examples.chinese: 莉莉[感谢朋友送了她漂亮的礼物]。

examples.english: We should [thank the teacher for helping us].
examples.chinese: 我们应该[谢谢老师帮了我们]。

synonyms: express gratitude to someone for something

meanings.explanation: If you [talk to] someone, you speak to them in order to communicate or have a conversation.

examples.english: I [talk to] my best friend every day after school.
examples.chinese: 我每天放学后都[跟好朋友聊天]。

examples.english: The doctor [talked to] my dad about eating more vegetables.
examples.chinese: 医生[跟我爸爸说了]要多吃蔬菜。

examples.english: Our class is [talking to] the new student from Japan.
examples.chinese: 我们班正在[跟日本来的新同学说话]。

meanings.explanation: If you [talk with] someone, you have a conversation with them, usually in a friendly way, to share news, ideas, or feelings.

examples.english: I like to [talk with] my grandma on the phone every Sunday.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢每个星期天在电话里和奶奶[聊天]。

examples.english: The teacher [talked with] my mom about my homework.
examples.chinese: 老师和我妈妈[谈了谈]我的作业。

examples.english: We sat in the park and [talked with] our new neighbors for an hour.
examples.chinese: 我们坐在公园里和新邻居[聊了]一个小时。

derived_forms: texted back (past tense and past participle)

meanings.explanation: When you [text back], you send a text message to someone in reply to the message they sent you.

examples.english: I’m waiting for my cousin to [text back] about our picnic plan.
examples.chinese: 我在等表姐[回短信]说我们野餐计划的事。

examples.english: After I got her party invitation, I [texted back] to say yes right away.
examples.chinese: 我收到她的派对邀请后，立刻[回短信]答应了。

examples.english: My little sister hasn't [texted back] to me yet—maybe she's playing outside.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹还没给我[回短信]——也许她在外面玩呢。

meanings.explanation: If you [throw away] something you do not want or need, you put it in a trash can or get rid of it.

examples.english: Please don't [throw away] that box; I can use it for my school project.
examples.chinese: 请别[扔掉]那个盒子，我可以用它来做学校的手工。

examples.english: Mom told me to [throw away] the old bread before it gets moldy.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我把变干的面包[扔掉]，不然会长毛。

examples.english: I accidentally [threw away] my homework, but the teacher gave me a new sheet.
examples.chinese: 我不小心[扔掉了]作业纸，还好老师又给了我一张新的。

meanings.explanation: If you [take away] something from a person or place, you remove it from there.

examples.english: The waiter [took away] our empty plates after lunch.
examples.chinese: 午饭后服务员[收走]了我们的空盘子。

examples.english: Please don't [take away] my favorite teddy bear.
examples.chinese: 请不要[拿走]我最爱的泰迪熊。

examples.english: The teacher [took away] Jack's toy car because he played with it in class.
examples.chinese: 老师[收走]了杰克的玩具车，因为他在课堂上玩。

common_collocations: try on shoes in the store
try on a dress / hat / coat

meanings.explanation: If you [try on] a piece of clothing, shoes, or accessories, you put them on to see if they fit you properly or look good on you.

examples.english: Can I [try on] this red sweater, please?
examples.chinese: 请问我可以[试穿]这件红色毛衣吗？

examples.english: She [tried on] three hats but didn't like any of them.
examples.chinese: 她[试戴]了三顶帽子，但一顶也不喜欢。

examples.english: Mom told me to [try on] the new shoes at home.
examples.chinese: 妈妈让我在家[试穿]那双新鞋。

meanings.explanation: When you [tidy up], you make a place neat by putting all your things back in their proper places.

examples.english: After playing with my toys, I always [tidy up] the playroom.
examples.chinese: 玩完玩具后，我总会[收拾好]游戏室。

examples.english: Yesterday I [tidied up] my bedroom before my cousin came to visit.
examples.chinese: 昨天我在表弟来之前[整理好了]我的卧室。

examples.english: Our teacher asks us to [tidy up] our desks before going home.
examples.chinese: 老师让我们放学前[整理好]自己的书桌。

meanings.explanation: When you [turn in] something, you give it to the person who is supposed to receive it, such as a teacher, a boss, or an official.

examples.english: I need to [turn in] my math homework before class starts.
examples.chinese: 我必须在上课前[交]数学作业。

examples.english: Please [turn in] your permission slip to your teacher tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 请明天把家长同意书[交给]老师。

examples.english: Tom [turned in] his book report right on time.
examples.chinese: 汤姆准时[交了]他的读书报告。

derived_forms: turn-off (noun: road exit or unappealing feature)

meanings.explanation: When you [turn off] a piece of electrical equipment or a gas supply, you stop it from working by using a switch or button.

examples.english: Before I go to bed, I always [turn off] my bedroom light.
examples.chinese: 睡觉前，我总会[关掉]卧室的灯。

examples.english: Mom asked me to [turn off] the TV because it's time for dinner.
examples.chinese: 妈妈叫我[关掉]电视，因为该吃晚饭了。

examples.english: Dad [turned off] the car engine when we arrived at the park.
examples.chinese: 爸爸到公园后[关掉]了汽车引擎。

derived_forms: turn-on (n., informal: something or someone that excites you)

meanings.explanation: To [turn on] a device, machine, or light means to make it start working, usually by pressing a button, flipping a switch, or turning a tap.

examples.english: Please [turn on] the light. I can't see anything in the dark.
examples.chinese: 请把灯[打开]，我什么都看不见。

examples.english: I [turned on] the TV to watch my favorite cartoon after school.
examples.chinese: 放学后我[打开]了电视，看我最喜欢的动画片。

examples.english: Mom [turns on] the radio every morning while making breakfast.
examples.chinese: 妈妈每天早上做早饭时都会[打开]收音机。

common_collocations: wake sb up in the morning
wake sb up from a nap
wake sb up with a kiss

meanings.explanation: If you [wake someone up], you cause them to stop sleeping and become conscious.

examples.english: Please [wake me up] at seven o'clock tomorrow morning.
examples.chinese: 请明天早上七点[叫醒我]。

examples.english: Mom [wakes my sister up] every day before school.
examples.chinese: 妈妈每天上学前[叫醒我妹妹]。

examples.english: The loud thunder [woke the baby up] last night.
examples.chinese: 昨晚那声巨雷[吵醒了宝宝]。

meanings.explanation: To [walk along] means to move forward on foot beside something, like a road, a river, or a beach, following its direction.

examples.english: We [walked along] the beach and found some pretty shells.
examples.chinese: 我们沿着海滩[走]，捡到了一些漂亮的贝壳。

examples.english: Every morning, Grandma likes to [walk along] the river near her house.
examples.chinese: 每天早上，奶奶都喜欢在她家附近的河边[走走]。

examples.english: Let's [walk along] this street and see what shops are here.
examples.chinese: 我们沿着这条街[走走吧]，看看都有什么店。

meanings.explanation: If you [wake up], you stop sleeping and become awake again.

examples.english: Every morning, I [wake up] when my alarm clock rings.
examples.chinese: 每天早上，闹钟响的时候我就[醒来]。

examples.english: Yesterday morning, I [woke up] an hour later than usual.
examples.chinese: 昨天早上，我比平常[醒来]晚了一个小时。

examples.english: My little sister always asks Mom to [wake her up] when we go camping.
examples.chinese: 我们去露营时，我妹妹总让妈妈[叫她起床]。

meanings.explanation: If you [work on] something, you spend time and effort trying to do it, improve it, or solve it.

examples.english: I need to [work on] my handwriting so it looks neater.
examples.chinese: 我需要[练一练]我的字，让它看起来更工整。

examples.english: My dad is [working on] fixing the broken bike in the garage.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸正在车库里[修]那辆坏掉的自行车。

examples.english: She [worked on] her science project all weekend.
examples.chinese: 她整个周末都在[做]她的科学小项目。

meanings.explanation: When you [turn down] a device like a radio, TV, or heater, you make it quieter or less hot.

examples.english: Can you [turn down] the TV? I'm doing my homework.
examples.chinese: 你能把电视[调小]一点吗？我正在写作业。

examples.english: My mom [turned down] the heat because the room was too warm.
examples.chinese: 我妈妈把暖气[调小]了，因为房间太热了。

examples.english: Please [turn down] your music—it's too loud!
examples.chinese: 请把你的音乐[调小]一点——太吵啦！

meanings.explanation: If you [wait for] someone or something, you stay where you are until that person comes or that thing happens.

examples.english: I [wait for] the school bus at the bus stop every morning.
examples.chinese: 我每天早上在公交站[等]校车。

examples.english: Please [wait for] me — I'll be ready soon.
examples.chinese: 请[等]我——我马上就准备好了。

examples.english: The children [waited for] the rain to stop before playing outside.
examples.chinese: 孩子们[等]雨停了才出去玩耍。

meanings.explanation: If you [think of] someone or something, you bring that person or thing into your mind.

examples.english: I [thought of] my grandma when I saw this photo.
examples.chinese: 看到这张照片时，我[想到了]奶奶。

examples.english: Can you [think of] a good name for my new kitten?
examples.chinese: 你能给我的小猫咪[想出]一个好名字吗？

examples.english: I'm [thinking of] what to eat for lunch.
examples.chinese: 我正在[想]中午吃什么。

meanings.explanation: When you [work out], you do physical activities to keep your body healthy and strong.

examples.english: My dad [works out] at the gym three times a week.
examples.chinese: 我爸爸每周在健身房[锻炼]三次。

examples.english: I [worked out] with my mom in our living room this morning.
examples.chinese: 我今天早上和妈妈在客厅[锻炼]了。

examples.english: Lily enjoys [working out] with her dad in the park on Sundays.
examples.chinese: 莉莉喜欢周日和她爸爸在公园里[锻炼]。

meanings.explanation: If you [take care of] someone or something, you do what is needed to keep them safe, healthy, and well looked after.

examples.english: I help my mom [take care of] our pet cat every day.
examples.chinese: 我每天帮妈妈[照顾]我们的宠物猫。

examples.english: When my parents go out, my grandma [takes care of] me.
examples.chinese: 我爸妈出门的时候，奶奶[照顾]我。

examples.english: My cousin [took care of] our neighbor's goldfish while they were on holiday.
examples.chinese: 邻居一家去度假时，我的表哥[照看]他们的金鱼。

meanings.explanation: To [think about] something means to spend time considering it in your mind, or to have an idea of someone or something in your thoughts.

examples.english: I am [thinking about] what to draw next.
examples.chinese: 我正在[考虑]接下来画什么。

examples.english: What do you [think about] this new game?
examples.chinese: 你觉得这个新游戏[怎么样]？

examples.english: Mum [thinks about] us all the time.
examples.chinese: 妈妈一直[惦记着]我们。

meanings.explanation: When you [walk to] a place, you move your feet one step at a time to go there.

examples.english: Every day I [walk to] school with my sister.
examples.chinese: 我每天和妹妹一起[走到]学校。

examples.english: We [walked to] the park after dinner.
examples.chinese: 晚饭后我们[走到]公园。

examples.english: My grandpa [walks to] the bookstore every Sunday.
examples.chinese: 我爷爷每个星期天[走到]书店。

meanings.explanation: If you [write to] someone, you send them a letter, card, or email to give them news or ask for something.

examples.english: I [write to] my grandma every week to tell her about school.
examples.chinese: 我每周都[写信给]奶奶，告诉她学校的事。

examples.english: Tom [wrote to] Santa and asked for a new bike.
examples.chinese: 汤姆[写信给]圣诞老人，想要一辆新自行车。

examples.english: She is [writing to] her cousin in Canada right now.
examples.chinese: 她正在[写信给]她在加拿大的表姐。

meanings.explanation: To [worry about] something means to keep thinking about it and feel unhappy or nervous because something bad might happen.

examples.english: Don't [worry about] the rain. We can play inside today.
examples.chinese: 别[担心]下雨。我们今天可以在屋里玩。

examples.english: I always [worry about] my little sister when she walks to school alone.
examples.chinese: 小妹妹一个人走路去上学时，我总是很[担心]她。

examples.english: There is nothing to [worry about]. Everything will be fine!
examples.chinese: 没什么可[担心的]。一切都会好的！

meanings.explanation: When you [shop for] something, you go to stores to look at different things and choose the one you want to buy.

examples.english: Every Saturday, Mom goes to the supermarket to [shop for] our family's food.
examples.chinese: 每个周六，妈妈都会去超市[采购]我们家的食物。

examples.english: Last Sunday, I went to the mall to [shop for] a new pair of sneakers.
examples.chinese: 上周日，我去商场[选购]了一双新运动鞋。

examples.english: My older sister is [shopping for] a birthday gift for our grandma.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐正在[挑选]给奶奶的生日礼物。

meanings.explanation: If you [write down] something, you put it on paper using a pen or pencil so that you can remember it or keep a record of it.

examples.english: Please [write down] your name on the paper.
examples.chinese: 请在纸上[写下]你的名字。

examples.english: I [wrote down] the homework in my notebook.
examples.chinese: 我把作业[记]在了笔记本上。

examples.english: She is [writing down] the teacher's words.
examples.chinese: 她正在[记下]老师说的话。

meanings.explanation: If you [turn up] somewhere, you arrive there or appear there, often after people have been waiting for you.

examples.english: We waited for an hour, but Tom never [turned up].
examples.chinese: 我们等了一个小时，但汤姆始终没有[出现]。

examples.english: Lily [turned up] at school just before the bell rang.
examples.chinese: 莉莉在打铃前刚好[赶到]学校。

examples.english: My friend didn't [turn up] for my birthday party, so I was sad.
examples.chinese: 我的朋友没有[来]我的生日派对，所以我很难过。
